How to Onboard a New Employee

Responsible Teams and Roles
HR Operations, Hiring Manager, IT Support

New Employee Onboarding Runbook

Purpose
This runbook standardizes the preparation, day-one setup, and first-month enablement of new employees. It ensures that documentation, access, equipment, training, and role expectations are aligned before productive work begins.

When to Use
Use this runbook for all regular new hires and adapt as needed for temporary workers, interns, or internal transfers.

Responsible Roles
Primary owner: HR Operations.
Co-owners: Hiring Manager and IT Support.
Supporting roles: Payroll, Facilities, Department trainer.

Procedure
Step 1: Create the employee record in the HRIS after the signed offer is received and confirm start date, title, manager, location, and employment type.
Step 2: Launch the onboarding checklist and assign tasks to HR, IT, Payroll, and the hiring manager.
Step 3: Request equipment, email account, collaboration tools, and role-based systems access from IT.
Step 4: Verify completion of required pre-start forms, including identity verification, tax forms, direct deposit, confidentiality agreements, and policy acknowledgments.
Step 5: Review the packet one business day before start and escalate any missing documentation.
Step 6: Prepare the day-one agenda with welcome meeting, team introduction, policy orientation, and technical access validation.
Step 7: On day one, confirm the employee can log in, enroll in MFA, access key tools, and locate core policies and support contacts.
Step 8: During week one, track mandatory compliance training, department training, and manager check-ins.
Step 9: By day 30, review onboarding completion, role readiness, and any enablement gaps needing corrective action.
Step 10: Archive the completed checklist and note any lessons learned if delays or access issues occurred.

Approval Requirements
Standard onboarding does not require manager approval beyond hiring confirmation.
Access to privileged or regulated systems requires data-owner or security approval.
Employees may not begin customer-data or payment-related work until required compliance documentation is complete.

Quality Controls
HR audits sample onboarding records monthly for completeness.
Managers must confirm role-specific training completion before assigning independent production work.

Completion Criteria
Onboarding is complete when required documents are validated, access is working, training milestones are recorded, and the employee is cleared for normal role duties.
